items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...especially of the older drummers, like yourself and Jo Jones and Buddy Rich and Louie Bellson had been professional caliber tap dancers.

ctx.x: Hips" Tucker, There was another Snake Hips around then, a very nice looking one. He never made it quite as big as this Earl. There was another one round there could do it just as well as he did.
While we're on the subject of dancers, why is it that so many, especially of the older drummers, like yourself and Jo Jones and Buddy Rich and Louie Bellson had been professional caliber tap dancers.
I don't know. I imagine that's how I first got started was just tap dancing like that, and then--

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: When we get there you know good and well that Cozy and I were hanging out.

ctx.x: No, the big band, and Johnson was on bass, and Coottie was there, you see. So what happened was everybody made a change but me. J. C. switched from Teddy, from Cafe Society, to go to play with Cab. Meanwhile you were right there in California when we Big Log Chicken and I said, "Cozy, you going to have to go on the staff and play with Raymond Scott." Cab didn't want him to leave. I said, "You have to leave, Fess, because we have to make a move out of here. You can't get Sidney; you'll have to take J. C." So J. C.…

items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I knew a little drummer by the name of Cees.

ctx.x: You see, the thing of it is I had to go to Washington. I knew a little drummer by the name of Cees. So Tommy Potter and all the guys, John Malachi, all of the guys were going down to the Crystal Cavern. I'd go down there and hang around with them and sit down in a little restaurant, sit down and talk about things to come. I'd say, "Now you're going to grow up and when you come to New York, look me up. Go around and hang out with so-and-so and learn," because they had a couple of drummers around there, just doing…
